fresh_refs.title: Evidence of Potential Thermospheric Overcooling During the May 2024 Geomagnetic Superstorm
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Open-access arxiv paper (2411.14071) directly quantifying Gannon storm thermosphere response: Swarm-A/C observed ~300% peak density enhancement at ~462-500 km, followed by a -22% to -23% post-storm depletion on May 12. Establishes that geomagnetic forcing (Dst -412 nT) dominated EUV during storm main phase despite continuous EUV increase. NO infrared cooling reached an 'all-time high' of 11.84 ergs/cm2/sec. Critical ground truth for the frame-flip observable: quiet pre-storm period has F10.7 as background driver; storm main phase flips to Dst/geomagnetic dominance.

fresh_refs.title: Satellite Drag Analysis During the May 2024 Gannon Geomagnetic Storm (Parastoo et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Open-access (arxiv 2406.08617, AIAA). Confirms density enhancements up to 6x baseline at 400 km within 12 hours of storm onset using TLE/NORAD catalog and GRACE-FO/TerraSAR-X POD. Quantifies that even one-day-ahead forecasts failed to predict storm magnitude. The 6x enhancement at ~400-500 km altitude over ~12 hours sets the temporal and spatial scale for the GRACE-FO/Swarm data your instrument will use.

fresh_refs.title: GOLD Observations of the Thermospheric Response to the 10-12 May 2024 Gannon Superstorm (Evans et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: GRL paper analyzing UV remote-sensing of thermosphere composition and temperature during Gannon. Uses independent optical observations (not POD), providing cross-validation for density enhancements. Relevant because it constrains the altitude-integrated column, which is complementary to the point-altitude POD measurements your instrument uses.

fresh_refs.title: High-Latitude Electrodynamics and Thermospheric Density Variations During the 2024 Gannon Storm (Zhu et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: 2026 Space Weather paper (10.1029/2025SW004699) directly addresses high-latitude electrodynamics contribution to Gannon density variations. Finds that accurate representation of high-latitude electrodynamics is essential to reproduce storm-time density — relevant because it separates the Joule heating mechanism (geomagnetic driver) from the EUV background. Key for the frame-flip design: confirms geomagnetic input quality matters most during storm.

fresh_refs.title: Impact of Solar Irradiance on Storm-Time Thermospheric Mass Density Response (Zhang et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: GRL 2026 paper (10.1029/2025GL120471). Uses ensemble simulations varying F10.7 preconditioning before the 2015 St. Patrick's Day storm. Directly tests the F10.7 vs Dst interaction question: EUV (F10.7) sets the background state (preconditioning), while geomagnetic forcing drives storm-time density increments. This is the clearest recent evidence that the two drivers are NOT purely additive — F10.7 level modulates how much density the geomagnetic forcing produces. Forces design change: the additive baseline must include an interaction or the interaction term must be explicitly tested.

fresh_refs.title: Investigating Magnetosphere-Ionosphere-Thermosphere Coupling During Geomagnetic Storms With a Novel Thermospheric Disturbance Index (Wu et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: JGR Space Physics 2026 (10.1029/2025JA034887). Introduces a new index Jp^T to quantify thermospheric disturbance independently of existing geomagnetic indices. Relevant for the instrument because this new index could serve as a cleaner geomagnetic driver variable for the synergy gate, reducing index-to-index cross-correlation that contaminates F10.7/Dst decomposition.

fresh_refs.title: Thermospheric Density Variations During Extreme Geomagnetic Storms and Their Potential Impact on the Orbit of the China Space Station (Frontiers 2025)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Open-access Frontiers paper across storms 1989/2003/2015. Shows that quiet-period background F10.7 (81-day average ~200 sfu in 1989 vs ~130 sfu in 2015) substantially amplifies density decay rates even during comparable Dst storms. Quantifies this: model bias toward NRLMSIS 2.0 is partially explained by elevated F10.7. Confirms the preconditioning interaction is real and measurable across multiple storms.

fresh_refs.title: A Survey of Current Operations-Ready Thermospheric Density Models for Drag Modeling in LEO Operations (PMC12995994)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Open-access PMC survey. Confirms HASDM 2020-2025 extension 'expected to be publicly released early 2026' and a HASDM forecast database is being developed. At 550 km, existing models disagree by a factor of 2 under quiet conditions. Directly relevant to baseline model choice for the additive fit.

fresh_refs.title: SET HASDM Density Database 2020-2025 Extension (spacewx.com)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: The SET HASDM website now lists the 2020-2025 extension as available via the HASDM Database API (same specs: 1-hour local solar time resolution, 10 deg lat x 15 deg lon, 175-825 km at 25 km steps, free for research). The PMC survey (2025) confirms release was expected 'early 2026'. The spacewx.com page implies it is now live. This covers the Gannon storm window (May 2024) in the HASDM framework — though note this is HASDM1 (J70+corrections), not the full operational CSpOC algorithm.

fresh_refs.title: Evaluating F10.7 and F30 Radio Fluxes as Long-Term Solar Proxies of Energy Deposition in the Thermosphere (Annales Geophysicae 2025)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Open-access ANGEO paper. Shows F10.7 saturates during deep solar minima (overestimates EUV by ~8% vs F30's ~4% overestimate). During solar maximum (2024 context), F10.7 is a better proxy than at minimum. Key confound: if using 2024 data near solar maximum, F10.7 saturation is not the main issue, but the nonlinear relationship between F10.7 and actual EUV still introduces noise in the marginal model.

fresh_refs.title: A Machine Learning-Based Thermospheric Density Model with Uncertainty Quantification (MSIS-UN, Atmospheres 2025)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: ADS 2025Atmos..16.1120L. Extends NRLMSISE-00 with heteroscedastic neural networks and sparse PCA. Input set includes F10.7 and geomagnetic indices with standard lag windows. Relevant because it shows that adding uncertainty quantification to the marginal model reduces apparent model error — a direct design lesson for the additive baseline: the baseline must report calibration bands, not just point estimates.

fresh_refs.title: Improving Thermospheric Density Predictions in Low-Earth Orbit With Machine Learning (Acciarini et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Karman/thermoNET. Open-source (github.com/spaceml-org/karman). Reduces MAPE from 40-60% to ~20% over NRLMSISE-00/JB2008 using the same F10.7+geomagnetic inputs. Inputs include lagged geomagnetic indices alongside solar proxies. Important because Karman's data pipeline includes GRACE-FO/Swarm POD density, which is the same source as your instrument — their preprocessing choices (altitude normalization, orbit averaging) are directly reusable.

fresh_refs.title: Thermospheric Mass Density Derived in Near Real Time from Space Debris (Johlander et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: SWSC 2026 paper. Uses 2348 TLE debris objects 200-800 km, 2018-2024. Confirms May 2024 Gannon storm produced decay rate >4x at 490 km. Independently verifies the ~300-400% enhancement range. Uses F10.7, Dst, and Hp30 as drivers. Notes that the standard '81-day centered average' introduces a 45-day lag into solar forcing — this is a direct quantitative confound for the additive baseline design.

fresh_refs.title: Adaptive AI Forecasting of Thermospheric Neutral Density Tuned to GRACE Data (Thomsen and Foorotan, EGU 2026 abstract)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: EGU26-4384. XGBoost model achieving 60-70% RMSE reduction (quiet) and ~40% (storm) over NRLMSIS-2.1 by including lagged F10.7, Ap, and TEC as joint inputs. Explicitly uses 'lagged geomagnetic and ionospheric variables' — confirms that lag selection is an active research design choice, not fixed.

fresh_refs.title: JB2008 Lag Implementation Reference (DTIC/Bowman et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Canonical model defines the standard lag windows: F10.7 and S10 use 1-day lag; M10 uses 2-day lag; Y10 uses undisclosed best lag. Geomagnetic: 3-hour Ap. This is the baseline lag structure the s1_drag_synergy additive model must reproduce or explain deviating from. Critically: NRLMSISE-00 uses 81-day mean + previous-day F10.7 + 3h Ap — two different lag conventions for the same two driver families.

fresh_refs.title: Temporal Information Partitioning: Characterizing Synergy, Uniqueness, and Redundancy in Interacting Environmental Variables (Illinois Experts / Goodwell et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Applies partial information decomposition (PID) to environmental time series (air temperature, humidity, wind). Not yet applied to space weather, but directly applicable methodology: uses Rescaled Redundancy (Rs) to avoid source-dependency artifacts that inflate redundancy estimates. The key methodological lesson for s1: standard PID overestimates redundancy between correlated sources (F10.7 and Dst are correlated during active Sun periods), so the Rs correction is needed before calling a result 'synergy'.

fresh_refs.title: Partial Information Decomposition for Multivariate Gaussian Systems Based on Information Geometry (Entropy 2024)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: June 2024 Entropy paper presenting a Gaussian PID framework. Relevant because F10.7/Dst joint density can be approximated as bivariate Gaussian for quiet periods; the Gaussian PID gives closed-form synergy estimates that are checkable analytically. Provides a calibration check: run Gaussian PID on the quiet-sun window and verify it matches your MDL-based synergy gain.

fresh_refs.title: Reconstructing Historical Solar Indices for Predicting Past Space Weather Events (Belbase et al.)
fresh_refs.why_relevant: Space Weather 2026 (10.1029/2025SW004757). Addresses F10.7 data quality and reconstruction for historical events. Relevant because if F10.7 values for early 2024 have reconstruction uncertainty, it introduces noise into the marginal f(F10.7) fit that could either inflate or deflate apparent synergy.

design_changes: INTERACTION TERM REQUIRED IN ADDITIVE BASELINE: Zhang et al. 2026 (GRL) directly shows that F10.7 preconditioning modulates storm-time geomagnetic response in a nonlinear way. A strictly additive f(F10.7) + g(Dst) baseline may systematically underfit storm windows regardless of backfit quality, artificially inflating synergy gain. Required change: either (a) add an explicit F10.7 x Dst interaction term to the additive baseline and test whether synergy is above this extended baseline, or (b) report separate synergy estimates for quiet vs storm windows and note that the interaction is already partly captured in the literature.

LAG WINDOW MUST BE GRID-SEARCHED, NOT FIXED: Standard models disagree on lag: NRLMSISE uses previous-day F10.7 + 3h Ap; JB2008 uses 1-day F10.7, 2-day M10, 3h Ap; Karman/Thomsen use lagged windows as tunable hyperparameters. The Johlander 2026 debris paper shows that the 81-day centered average introduces a ~45-day lag into the solar proxy, which is completely different from the 1-day lag. Required change: for both f(F10.7) and g(Dst), the additive baseline must grid-search lag windows (candidates: 0h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 24h, 48h for Dst; 1-day, 81-day average for F10.7) and use the best-fit lags. The gain_v2 lesson is directly applicable: misspecified lag in the marginals will fake synergy.

QUIET-SUN WINDOW SHOULD EXCLUDE SOLAR-FLARE-ONLY DAYS: Gannon storm was preceded by multiple X-class flares beginning early May 2024. The 'quiet' flank (March-April 2024) still had elevated F10.7 (Solar Cycle 25 maximum approach). The quiet/storm window split must verify that the quiet flank has F10.7 consistent with true background and is not contaminated by pre-storm elevated EUV. Recommend using F10.7 < 150 sfu AND |Dst| < 30 nT as quiet-window criteria, verified against OMNI2 data.

DENSITY NORMALIZATION: ORBIT-AVERAGING IS INSUFFICIENT FOR ALTITUDE VARIATION: Swarm-C operated at 480-500 km during Gannon storm; GRACE-FO operated at 474-506 km. These are close but not identical. Density scales exponentially with altitude in this range (scale height ~50-80 km at these altitudes). A 30 km altitude difference introduces ~30-60% density difference, which is comparable to the quiet-time F10.7 signal. Required: either restrict to a single satellite (GRACE-FO or Swarm-C, not both pooled without correction), or apply an exponential altitude normalization using a reference atmosphere (e.g., NRLMSIS 2.1 ratio correction) before fitting the additive model.

LOCAL SOLAR TIME (LST) MUST BE INCLUDED AS COVARIATE OR AVERAGED OUT: POD density at a given orbit position reflects both the global storm response and the diurnal/semidiurnal tide at that LST. During the Gannon storm, Joule heating was predominantly high-latitude and asymmetric (northern hemisphere dominated during main phase). Including LST as a covariate in the additive baseline prevents the diurnal signal from aliasing into F10.7 or Dst terms. Alternative: use orbit-averaged density per pass (~90-min orbit), which reduces but does not eliminate LST dependence.

HEMISPHERIC ASYMMETRY IN GANNON STORM IS A KNOWN CONFOUND: Overcooling paper (2411.14071) documents that the post-storm depletion (-23%) was confined to the northern hemisphere; the southern hemisphere recovered without depletion. If GRACE-FO/Swarm data are not stratified by hemisphere, the quiet-recovery averaging will mix two physically distinct populations, smearing the Dst response function in the additive baseline and creating apparent model error falsely attributed to synergy.

HASDM 2020-2025 EXTENSION: USE AS SECONDARY VALIDATION, NOT PRIMARY DATA: The SET HASDM extension (2020-2025) is now publicly available via API and covers the Gannon storm window. However, HASDM1 uses J70 + temperature corrections derived from satellite drag, which introduces a model-dependent density estimate (not purely observational). GRACE-FO and Swarm POD remain the primary ground truth. HASDM can be used as an independent second dataset to cross-check synergy findings, with the caveat that HASDM is itself a model and may suppress or impose specific driver correlations.

NO PUBLISHED PID/SYNERGY APPLICATION TO THERMOSPHERE EXISTS: The literature search found zero papers applying partial information decomposition or formal synergy measures to thermospheric density or space weather drivers. This is a genuine gap, not a sign that the idea is wrong. It means the instrument has no external benchmark for 'expected synergy magnitude' in this domain. Required change: add a calibration experiment using a synthetic dataset (known F10.7 + Dst + interaction term) to verify that the compression-gain method correctly recovers known synergy magnitudes before applying to real data.

F10.7 SATURATION NEAR SOLAR MAXIMUM: F10.7 reaches a nonlinear saturation regime above ~200 sfu during Solar Cycle 25 maximum (2024). The Tapping/Mandrini 2025 paper shows F30 is a more linear EUV proxy at high activity. If the study window (March-July 2024) includes F10.7 > 180 sfu days (likely during the Gannon pre-storm flare sequence), the marginal f(F10.7) fit using a linear or log-linear model will be misspecified. Required: check the F10.7 distribution in the study window from OMNI2 and log-transform or cap if skewed above 200 sfu.

NRLMSIS 2.1 BIAS HAS DOCUMENTED F10.7 DEPENDENCE: The PMC survey and multiple 2025-2026 papers note that NRLMSIS 2.1 storm-time bias is statistically correlated with F10.7. This means if the additive baseline is initialized from NRLMSIS outputs (as in many correction-model approaches), the residual will inherit an artificial F10.7 correlation that does not represent true F10.7 information content. Recommended fix: fit the additive model directly to POD density observations, not to NRLMSIS residuals.
known_confounds: ALTITUDE-DENSITY EXPONENTIAL SCALING: The ~30 km altitude variation between GRACE-FO and Swarm-C orbits during 2024 introduces ~30-60% density variation at these altitudes (scale height 50-80 km at 400-500 km). Not controlling for altitude will inflate residuals and could masquerade as unexplained variance attributable to the joint term. Mitigation: normalize all densities to a fixed reference altitude (e.g., 450 km) using the NRLMSIS 2.1 ratio rho_ref/rho_model before any regression.

LOCAL SOLAR TIME (DIURNAL TIDE) ALIASING: POD density at each orbit point carries a diurnal density wave with amplitude ~20-50% at these altitudes. The diurnal wave is driven by solar EUV (correlated with F10.7) but not by Dst. If data are not orbit-averaged or LST is not included as a covariate, the diurnal signal will leak into the f(F10.7) marginal, inflating its explained variance and suppressing apparent synergy.

F10.7-Dst CORRELATION DURING ACTIVE SUN: During solar maximum, active regions produce both elevated EUV (high F10.7) and increased CME/CIR frequency (elevated Dst events). F10.7 and |Dst| are positively correlated over multi-week timescales in 2024. Standard PID frameworks (Williams-Beer, Goodwell Rs) overestimate redundancy when sources are correlated. This means naive information-decomposition will attribute more to 'redundancy' and less to 'synergy' than is physically justified. Mitigation: use the Goodwell Rs correction or the Gaussian PID closed form as calibration.

LAG MISSPECIFICATION: The F10.7 driver response to density has two timescales: the immediate EUV heating response (hours, controlling by direct photoionization and heating) and the thermospheric composition adjustment response (1-2 days, O/N2 ratio changes). If only a single lag is used for F10.7, the marginal f(F10.7) will be misspecified and will leave predictable residuals that could be absorbed by the joint term and called synergy. The additive baseline must include both daily F10.7 and the 81-day average F10.7 as separate terms to capture both timescales. Geomagnetic response (Dst/Kp) is faster: 0-6 hours for Joule heating onset.

PRECONDITIONING (F10.7 x Dst INTERACTION): Zhang et al. 2026 shows F10.7 background level modulates storm-time Dst response. A high-F10.7 background (as in 2024 solar maximum) produces larger density enhancements for the same Dst minimum than a low-F10.7 background. This is a physical interaction, not pure synergy in the information-theoretic sense. The compression gain will capture it as synergy unless the additive baseline explicitly includes an F10.7 x Dst product term. This is the most important confound for the synergy gate claim.

HEMISPHERIC ASYMMETRY AND NORTHERN BIAS OF GANNON RESPONSE: The Gannon storm main-phase density enhancement was concentrated in the northern hemisphere (high-latitude Joule heating during May, when the northern hemisphere tilt favored auroral oval penetration deeper in latitude). Post-storm overcooling was also northern-hemisphere-only. If the satellite ground track is not stratified by hemisphere, storm-phase and recovery-phase signals are mixed, distorting the Dst response function in the additive model and potentially showing apparent synergy in the residuals.

MODEL-BASED DENSITY ESTIMATES VS. DIRECT ACCELEROMETER: GRACE-FO and Swarm-C provide accelerometer-derived density (direct). TLE/TND datasets are model-mediated (require an assumed ballistic coefficient and atmospheric model in the inversion). The Johlander 2026 debris TLE method has 12-20 hour resolution, much coarser than the 30-second GRACE-FO accelerometer resolution. If TND/TLE data are mixed with accelerometer data in the same regression, the different noise floors and temporal resolutions will produce heteroscedastic residuals that confound the compression gain measure.

SWARM-C ORBIT DRIFT IN LOCAL SOLAR TIME: Swarm-C (and Swarm-A/B) precess in local solar time slowly (~130 days for full LST coverage). During the 5-month study window (March-July 2024), Swarm-C's LST sampling is not uniform. This means that within the quiet-sun window, different calendar months sample different LSTs, introducing a systematic LST-season confound into the marginal fits if not explicitly controlled.

F10.7 PROXY NONLINEARITY ABOVE 200 SFU: During the Gannon pre-storm flare sequence (May 8-10 2024), F10.7 may have reached >200 sfu. Above this level, F10.7 saturates as an EUV proxy (Tapping 2025 shows ~8% overestimate relative to F30). A linear marginal f(F10.7) will fit poorly in this regime, generating residuals that the joint model can absorb. Mitigation: log-transform F10.7 or use F30 if available in the OMNI2 data for 2024.

POST-STORM OVERCOOLING AS A THIRD REGIME: The Gannon storm shows three dynamical regimes: (1) quiet pre-storm background (F10.7 dominant), (2) storm main phase (Dst dominant), (3) post-storm overcooling (NO infrared cooling elevated 2-4x, density falls below pre-storm despite elevated EUV). The third regime is not well captured by any additive model of F10.7 + Dst because the cooling mechanism (NO emission) is driven by storm history, not instantaneous Dst. A regression that pools all three regimes will find poor additive fit across the transition, and the compression gain of the joint model will partly reflect regime identification rather than true synergy.

data.density_source: TU Delft thermosphere data portal, version_02c GRACE-FO 1 (GRACE C), accelerometer-derived neutral density. Five monthly ZIP files: GC_DNS_ACC_2024_03_v02c.zip through GC_DNS_ACC_2024_07_v02c.zip. URLs: http://thermosphere.tudelft.nl/data/data/version_02/GRACE-FO_data/GC_DNS_ACC_2024_{03..07}_v02c.zip. License: CC BY 4.0. Reference: Siemes et al., J. Space Weather Space Clim. 2023. Native cadence: 10 s. 1,312,801 raw rows parsed, all flag==0 (no flagged samples). Time system: GPS, shifted -18 s to UTC. PANGAEA fallback was NOT needed.
data.driver_source: NASA SPDF OMNI2 hourly low-resolution, omni2_2024.dat. URL: https://spdf.gsfc.nasa.gov/pub/data/omni/low_res_omni/omni2_2024.dat. Format spec: https://spdf.gsfc.nasa.gov/pub/data/omni/low_res_omni/omni2.text. Fields extracted: F10.7 sfu (word 51, daily value replicated hourly by source), Dst nT (word 41, Kyoto), Kp*10 (word 39), Ap nT (word 50). 8784 lines = 366 days x 24 h (2024 leap year). Zero OMNI2 fill values (99/99999/999/999.9) found in the study window. F10.7_81d = centered 81-day mean of the daily series, computed from full-year 2024 file (window DOY 61..213 fully covered).
data.normalization_choice: ORBIT-AVERAGE (v0): primary density column is the source's running orbit-average density (column 10 of TU Delft file, flag==0 only). One ~94-min GRACE-FO orbit sweeps both LST sectors and the full along-orbit altitude range, so orbit-averaging is the v0 mitigation for both the LST/diurnal-tide aliasing confound and the within-orbit altitude confound. Point density (col 9) is retained as a secondary column for MODEL seat comparison. NO fixed-altitude renormalization applied (model-free chain); hourly mean altitude is kept as a covariate column (range 479.8-500.3 km, spread 20.5 km). The 20.5 km altitude spread introduces ~25-35% density variation at these altitudes (scale height ~60-70 km) and is disclosed as a remaining confound for the MODEL seat to handle (e.g., NRLMSIS ratio correction). Hemispheric stratification NOT done in v0 (Gannon N/S asymmetry confound disclosed; raw 10-s files cached for re-binning).
caveats: Altitude not renormalized to fixed reference: GRACE-FO altitude range 479.8-500.3 km (spread 20.5 km). Scale height ~60-70 km at these altitudes implies ~25-35% density variation from altitude alone. Orbit-average channel mitigates within-orbit altitude variation but not the secular orbit decay or storm-time orbital contraction. MODEL seat should apply NRLMSIS 2.1 ratio correction or include alt_mean_m as a covariate.

F10.7 outlier: 2024-07-30 daily value = 412.9 sfu (only day above 250 sfu in window; consistent with radio-burst contamination of the Ottawa/Penticton daily 10.7 cm measurement). F10.7_81d on that day = 227.7 sfu (outlier absorption). MODEL seat should log-transform F10.7 or exclude/cap the 2024-07-30 point. F10.7 > 200 sfu for 1200 of 3672 hours (solar-max saturation regime for EUV proxy).

F10.7 elevated during storm main phase: during the Gannon storm main phase (Dst < -200 nT, 22 hours), F10.7 was 218-227.9 sfu -- significantly above the quiet background (111.7-149.8 sfu). The two drivers are NOT in cleanly separated regimes during the storm. The strict quiet window (F10.7 < 150 AND |Dst| < 30) has 754 hours, concentrated in March-April 2024.

Hemispheric asymmetry: Gannon storm N/S density asymmetry (post-storm overcooling confined to N. hemisphere per Overcooling paper 2411.14071) is NOT controlled in v0. GRACE-FO ground track pools both hemispheres in the hourly mean. Raw 10-s files are cached for re-binning by hemisphere if needed.

LST: orbit-average mitigates but does not fully eliminate local-solar-time aliasing. Swarm-C LST precesses ~130 days for full coverage. This dataset uses GRACE-FO only (no Swarm pooling), so LST variation is contained within GRACE-FO's precession rate (~44 days/full LST cycle for GRACE-FO at this altitude). Hourly LST circular mean is provided as a covariate column.

Lag structure not applied in the aligned CSV: raw coincident alignment (lag=0) for all drivers. MODEL/synergy seats must grid-search lags (0h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 24h, 48h for Dst; 1-day and 81-day for F10.7) per gain_v2 discipline. Misspecified lags in the marginals will fake apparent synergy.

Interaction term: Zhang et al. 2026 (GRL) shows F10.7 preconditioning modulates storm-time Dst response nonlinearly. The additive baseline f(F10.7)+g(Dst) may systematically underfit storm windows. MODEL seat should test an explicit F10.7 x Dst product term in the baseline.
Single 24-hour density gap: 2024-07-12T12Z to 2024-07-13T11Z (24 rows missing density, all drivers present). Located far from the Gannon storm. Total: 3648 complete rows out of 3672 grid hours.
Data is real fetched from authoritative sources: TU Delft (CC BY 4.0, accelerometer-derived, not model-mediated) and NASA SPDF OMNI2. No fabricated values. data.real = true for all records.

synergy_delta.note: negative = additive wins; interaction term hurts

gate.synergy_verdict: NO SYNERGY. ANTI-SYNERGY. The JOINT model (additive + F10.7 x Dst interaction) is worse than the proper additive baseline in ALL 6 engine cells (3 lag budgets x 2 model families), by both NLL and LZMA scoring, even BEFORE accounting for model-bit cost. The interaction term hurts the held-out data fit by 1753 bits (L-med|lin) independently of parameter penalty. Synergy delta NLL = -2073 bits / -0.58 b/h, 95% CI = [-4457, -468] bits entirely on the anti-synergy side. Permutation floor p95 = -272 bits; observed delta is well inside the anti-synergy tail. The most likely mechanism is the misspecification confound disclosed by the DATA seat: F10.7 was elevated (218-228 sfu) during the Gannon storm main phase (Dst < -200 nT, 22 h), so the F10.7 x Dst product term conflates two simultaneously elevated additive drivers with genuine multiplicative coupling. The proper additive law captures the driver structure; the interaction adds only noise. Calibration note: joint residual autocorrelation rho1 = 0.983 means hourly residuals are far from iid; absolute bit values are inflated but the additive > joint ordering is stable under this shared confound.
gate.frame_flip_verdict: FLIP CONFIRMED in linear cells, UNRELIABLE in quadratic cells. In all three linear lag configurations (L-small, L-med, L-large): QUIET FLANKS are F10.7-dominated (ratio 3-7:1; quiet_pre ratio = 6.8:1 at +0.91 vs +0.13 bits/h); GANNON STORM WEEK flips to Dst-dominated (ratio 3.9:1; +0.50 vs +0.13 bits/h at L-med|lin). The reversal is qualitative and unanimous across lag budgets for linear models. Quiet_post (June-July) remains F10.7-dominant (+0.40 b/h) but at reduced strength vs pre-storm, consistent with solar activity still elevated post-storm. Quadratic cells are disqualified for the storm window: Dst quad terms catastrophically overfit the Dst = -406 nT extreme, producing nonsensical storm-window scores (e.g. Dst marginal costs 154-314 b/h in quad cells during storm). The within-storm window refit (7 alternate 24h blocks, n=168) corroborates direction only: Dst less negative than F10.7 (-3.93 vs -4.90 b/h), consistent with Dst dominance but with very sparse holdout. The -50 nT quiet threshold sensitivity confirms the dominance pattern is robust to threshold choice. CAVEATS: storm window n=168 (one week); exact ratios have large uncertainty; F10.7 co-elevation during storm means the storm flip partly reflects reduced F10.7 marginal value (already absorbed) not only Dst gain.
caveats: Altitude not renormalized: GRACE-FO range 479.8-500.3 km (20.5 km spread, scale height 60-70 km => 25-35% density variation from altitude alone). Altitude covariate included in every model; secular orbit decay and storm-time contraction not fully controlled.

F10.7 elevated during Gannon storm main phase (218-228 sfu vs 112-150 sfu quiet flanks): the F10.7 x Dst product term conflates two simultaneously elevated additive drivers with genuine multiplicative coupling -- the prime misspecification confound per gain_v2 discipline; likely cause of the anti-synergy reading.
F10.7 outlier 2024-07-30 (412.9 sfu, probable radio burst) capped at 300 sfu before log-transform.

Joint residual autocorrelation rho1 = 0.983 at hourly lag: absolute NLL values inflated for all models; relative ordering (additive vs joint) is stable under this shared confound. Block bootstrap L=72h partially corrects CIs.

Storm window n=168 (one calendar week): frame-flip dominance direction is consistent across lag configs but exact bits/h ratios carry large uncertainty. Within-storm refit has only 7 alternate-block folds (exploratory only).

Quadratic model cells are not load-bearing for the storm-window frame flip: Dst^2 term catastrophically overfits the extreme Dst = -406 nT event; storm-window quad scores are uninterpretable (e.g. Dst saves -154 to -314 b/h).
LZMA synergy delta is at resolution floor (672-bit steps) for some cells (L-med|lin = 0.0 bits exactly); NLL view is the more continuous and reliable scorer in this regime.
Hemisphere not stratified: Gannon storm N/S density asymmetry (overcooling confined to N. hemisphere) pools both hemispheres in the orbit-average channel; raw 10-s files cached for re-binning.
Single 24-hour density gap 2024-07-12/13 excluded via dropna; far from storm window.
All data real: TU Delft CC BY 4.0 accelerometer-derived density + NASA SPDF OMNI2. data.real = true. No fabricated values anywhere in the chain.

assumption_audit: "Two drivers" may be a miscarving of a single causal upstream. F10.7 and Dst are not independent causes sitting side by side; they are both downstream projections of a single solar state. The sun's magnetic-cycle and activity level produce photon output (EUV, indexed by F10.7) and particle/field output (the CME/solar-wind pressure that drives ring-current injection, indexed by Dst). These two outputs are not thermodynamically independent: an X-class flare and the CME that follows it from the same active region share a common parent event. The Gannon storm is exactly this case — the same region responsible for the elevated F10.7 (218–228 sfu) also produced the CME that drove Dst to -406 nT. What the synergy gate measured was not 'the coupling between two causes' but the information-theoretic shadow of a common-cause structure. The test that would distinguish them: simulate a counter-factual scenario where Dst spikes without F10.7 elevation (a 'stealth CME' from a low-activity sun) and where F10.7 spikes without Dst response (radio-noise outlier, as seen in the 412.9 sfu July 30 event capped in this very run). If those cases show the same synergy pattern, the two-cause framing holds; if they collapse to a single-driver limit, the correct frame is one parent (solar state) with two observable projections. The data already contains partial evidence: the 412.9 sfu outlier was excluded as a measurement artifact; that exclusion obscures one of the most informative cells for this audit. The misspecification confound flagged in the synergy verdict (F10.7 elevated during the storm main phase) is not only a confound — it is positive evidence for the common-cause hypothesis.

The 'driver dominance flip' observable is in danger of being read as a property of the phenomenon when it may be a property of the marginal information structure. During quiet sun, Dst is near-stationary (almost no variance to explain); the F10.7 marginal captures the variance structure precisely because Dst is not varying. During the storm, F10.7's variance is already partially absorbed by the backfit, and Dst spikes into a regime with no training analog. The 'flip' may therefore be a change in the marginal information BUDGET — F10.7 saturates its contribution at high solar activity, Dst unsaturates — rather than a genuine dominance reversal in the causal mechanism. The correct test would hold the marginal variances fixed (e.g., restrict to hours where both drivers span matched variance ranges) and ask whether dominance still flips. The current data does not do this.

The lag structure embeds a hidden assumption about causality direction. The synergy gate allows lags up to 72 hours. But EUV density response is nearly instantaneous (minutes to hours), while geomagnetic storm main phase develops over 12–24 hours after CME arrival, and recovery is 2–7 days. By allowing equal lag budgets for both drivers, the instrument treats them as symmetric. They are not: F10.7 is a proxy for a slow, nearly-persistent driver (solar flux changes over days to weeks), while Dst is a proxy for an impulsive driver (ring current injection peaks and decays over hours to days). A lag budget that is optimal for Dst (hours) is too coarse for the EUV coupling and too short for the recovery. The additive backfit inherits this asymmetry from the lag grid, meaning the 'proper additive baseline' may itself be misspecified in a way that systematically underestimates the Dst marginal and overestimates F10.7's, biasing the dominance ratios.
reframes: The WELD reading: density|(F10.7,Dst) as a child wrapper. In the parents-produce-W_C formalism, a child wrapper W_C is not merely the function composition of its parents — it is the result of welding two parent laws such that the child inherits both membranes. The synergy gate result (anti-synergy: additive > joint in all 6 engine cells) is not a failure of the parents-produce-W_C frame; it is what the frame predicts when the weld is ADDITIVE. An additive weld is the cleanest possible case: each parent law contributes its compression independently, and the child's total compression is approximately the sum of the parents' contributions. The fact that the interaction term HURTS (costs 1753 bits at L-med|lin) says the weld is not only additive but ORTHOGONAL — the parents' information about density is nearly non-overlapping in this channel. The interaction term is attempting to model a weld-coupling that is not present; it finds noise. This is a strong, not weak, instance of parents-produce-W_C: the weld is confirmed as a clean additive join, which is the null case of the formalism and the hardest baseline to beat. Where the frame would be STRAINED is if neither parent compressed at all — if density|(F10.7) and density|(Dst) were both no better than null, the 'two parents welded into a child' narrative would be empty. That is not what happened: F10.7 marginal saves 0.55 b/h, Dst saves 0.11 b/h, and the additive backfit saves 0.61 b/h. The child exists and has both parents' membranes. The non-synergy says only that the parents are not entangled at this channel resolution; they weld cleanly without coupling.

Frame-relativity vs. regime change: is the distinction real or verbal? The protocol's attribution rule says frame-dial variance is an OBSERVABLE, not noise. The dominance flip — F10.7 dominant in quiet (ratio 6.8:1), Dst dominant in storm (ratio 3.9:1) — is confirmed across all three linear lag configurations. But here is where the philosopher must push: frame-relativity (in the protocol sense) means the same phenomenon reads differently depending on the observer's frame setting; regime change means the phenomenon itself has structurally changed. The question is whether the Gannon storm represents the instrument's frame window moving across a boundary in the phenomenon's state space, or whether the driver-coupling structure of thermospheric density is qualitatively different inside vs. outside the storm. These are NOT merely verbal. If it is frame-relativity, then the flip is recoverable — given the storm frame setting, an observer tuned to F10.7 finds less new information simply because Dst is now moving and absorbing residual density variance that F10.7 cannot explain. The information budget shifts, not the physics. If it is genuine regime change, then the coupling coefficients in the density physics (how much density increases per unit of EUV input, per unit of ring-current injection) are themselves functions of storm state — which would mean the linear backfit is doubly misspecified in the storm window. The data cannot distinguish these with 168 storm-window hours and a linear model. But the distinction has a test: if you fit the coupling coefficients separately for quiet and storm windows and the coefficients are different (not just the input variances), that is regime change. If the coefficients are the same but the input variances differ, that is frame-relativity. This experiment did not separate those. The protocol's attribution rule does not resolve the question; it names it.
questions: If F10.7 and Dst are both projections of a single solar-state variable, what is the minimum-entropy representation of that common parent, and does the density signal compress MORE against that latent parent than against either observable proxy? The test: factor the (F10.7, Dst) bivariate time series into a common component and an orthogonal residual (PCA, or a physical solar-state model), then run the synergy gate against the common component alone. If the common component explains the density variation and the orthogonal residuals add nothing, the two-driver frame was wrong from the start. This is the causal version of the misspecification audit and it is not done.

The joint residual autocorrelation rho1 = 0.983 is the loudest number in the results and it is treated as a caveat rather than a finding. What law DOES model the residual structure? The residuals of the best model (additive backfit) have 98.3% lag-1 autocorrelation — meaning the backfit is capturing maybe 2% of the available compression. A law that modeled even the gross residual structure (an AR(1) on the residuals, a longer-lag model, a thermospheric-response parametric with the known relaxation timescales of ~4–12 hours) would dominate the additive backfit. The question is not 'does the joint beat the additive' but 'what does the residual structure look like, and is it driver-lag-shaped (recoverable by longer lags), seasonal (orbit-altitude drift), or storm-hysteresis-shaped (recoverable only by a non-linear state variable)?'

Is the altitude covariate doing work, or is it absorbing the storm signal? The caveat notes a 20.5 km altitude spread and 25–35% implied density variation. During the Gannon storm, thermospheric expansion contracts the density scale height and shifts the iso-density surfaces — a satellite at 490 km is effectively at a lower relative altitude during a storm than during quiet conditions. If the altitude covariate is linear and static (same coefficient quiet and storm), it will systematically mis-correct the storm-time density, and the 'Dst compression' reading partly picks up this mis-correction. The test: run the instrument with altitude dropped and with altitude interacted with Dst (altitude*Dst term) and compare the frame-flip ratios. If they change sign, the altitude correction is confounded with the driver signal.
out_of_box_experiments: Run the synergy gate on the STEALTH CME population from DONKI (NASA Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information): stealth CMEs are geoeffective CMEs with no associated solar flare signature and therefore minimal F10.7 elevation. If a Dst storm without F10.7 co-elevation shows Dst compression comparable to the Gannon storm week, the two-driver frame is vindicated and the common-cause hypothesis is weakened. If stealth CMEs show near-zero Dst marginal improvement (Dst compresses density only when F10.7 is also elevated), the common-cause structure is likely doing most of the work and the two observable proxies are aliased. All data is publicly available: DONKI event list at https://kauai.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/search/ (auth-free REST JSON), OMNI2 Dst for the same windows, TU Delft density for whichever satellite was operational. This is a read-only, real-data-only, no-new-infrastructure experiment entirely within the existing instrument architecture. The result is a falsification target for the assumption-audit claim above.

Replace the F10.7 proxy with the FISM2 (Flare Irradiance Spectral Model 2) 1-nm-bin EUV irradiance data, available from LASP at https://lasp.colorado.edu/lisird/data/fism_flare_bands/ and https://lasp.colorado.edu/lisird/data/fism_daily_bands/ (auth-free). F10.7 is a ground-based radio proxy for EUV because EUV was hard to measure from the ground; it is correlated with EUV but not identical, and the correlation degrades during flare events. If FISM2 spectral EUV (particularly the 0–45 nm band that drives thermospheric heating) shows a larger marginal compression gain than F10.7, then the anti-synergy result is partly a proxy-quality artifact: the interaction term was trying to correct for F10.7's degraded proxy quality during the storm, not model genuine F10.7*Dst coupling. This experiment requires only swapping the F10.7 column for FISM2 daily averages (same temporal cadence), re-running the existing synergy_gate.py instrument with the new driver column, and reading the delta. If FISM2 marginal > F10.7 marginal AND the synergy delta becomes less negative, the conclusion shifts from 'no synergy' to 'no synergy detectable with the F10.7 proxy, proxy quality is a confound.' This changes the claim lifecycle from dead child to demoted-pending-better-proxy.

attacks.target: COLLINEARITY / COMMON-CAUSE: is synergy double-counting a shared driver?
attacks.detail: Two separate sub-questions with different verdicts. (A) Marginal double-counting: FAILS to reverse. Partial correlations r(log_rho, log_F107 | Dst) = +0.634 and r(log_rho, Dst | log_F107) = -0.630 -- both drivers carry large, independent signal once the other is conditioned out. The overall r(log_F107, Dst/100) = -0.129 is low; the additive backfit is genuine joint-OLS on [F|G] together, so there is no naive sum of separately-fitted marginals. The marginals are NOT double-counting. (B) Interaction term collinearity: SUCCEEDS in explaining the mechanism. VIF(Dst/100) = 1842, VIF(F107*Dst) = 1848. Root cause: fc_dev = log10(F107) - log10(180) has variance 0.0073 in quiet but only 0.0001 in the storm week (F107 is nearly constant at 218-228 sfu during Gannon; it is the QUIET periods where F107 varies). The interaction term F107*Dst is informationally near-collinear with Dst alone during 96% of the window. The eigendecomposition of the scaled design matrix shows the interaction direction has eigenvalue ~0 before ridge; ridge lambda adds 3.67, meaning the interaction coefficient is heavily shrunk toward zero by necessity. The 80.7% overlap (81% of Dst<-100 hours also have F107>200) confirms common-cause co-elevation during the one storm event. VERDICT: collinearity explains WHY the joint model fails (the interaction is near-redundant with Dst), but this is an argument FOR the anti-synergy verdict, not against it. It does not reverse the finding. The partial signal of both drivers in the marginal models survives. Strongest implication: the correct test for multiplicative coupling requires a stealth-CME comparison (Dst storm without F107 elevation) to disentangle the common-cause structure from genuine coupling.

attacks.target: DOF / MODEL-BITS: does the joint model's loss survive honest parameter accounting?
attacks.detail: The joint model is worse than the additive on raw held-out data NLL by 1,753 bits at L-med|lin BEFORE any model-bit penalty is applied (additive data NLL = 29,343 bits, joint data NLL = 31,097 bits). The protocol adds 320 extra model bits for the 5 interaction parameters (5 params * 32 b/param * 2 parities), bringing the total to -2,073 bits. But this accounting is irrelevant to the sign: even at 0 bits per parameter (free interaction), the joint loses. AIC would add 14 bits, BIC 59 bits -- neither changes the sign. Stricter MDL (e.g., 64 bits/param) would add 640 bits total extra for joint, making it even worse. The ridge regression is the key mechanism: with near-zero eigenvalue on the interaction direction (eigenvalue ~0 before ridge, 3.67 after), the ridge shrinks the interaction coefficients toward zero, making the joint model numerically close to the additive. The cross-validation then penalizes the interaction terms for overfitting the training fold. This verdict is robust to any reasonable parameter accounting convention.

attacks.target: LAGS: was the additive baseline given a fair lag budget?
attacks.detail: The lag budget is symmetric by construction. At L-med: additive uses F107 lags [0d, 1d, 2d, 81d] and Dst lags [0h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 24h]. The joint uses the identical F107 and Dst lag sets, plus interaction terms fc_dev * lag(Dst, h) for the same 5 Dst lag values. The interaction terms do NOT add any new lag horizon not already present in the additive Dst marginal. The backfit method is single joint-OLS on the concatenated [alt | F_block | G_block] design matrix, which is exactly the joint-least-squares / backfit required by gain_v2 discipline -- not the forbidden naive sum of separately-fitted marginals. L-large adds Dst lags out to 48h; L-small uses fewer lags; all three cells show the same anti-synergy sign. No lag asymmetry exists between additive and joint. The valid mask starts at hour 72 (max lag across all cells) to avoid NaN-induced edge effects, which is symmetric for all models.

attacks.target: PHYSICAL CONFOUNDS: altitude normalization, log-transform, storm composition change
attacks.detail: Three sub-questions. (A) Log-transform: correctly applied. Target is log10(rho_orbit), F107 is log10(min(F107, 300)), consistent with the known log-linear scaling of thermospheric density with EUV. This is not a confound. (B) Altitude: the 20.5 km GRACE-FO altitude spread implies 25-35% density variation from altitude alone (scale height 60-70 km). Altitude is included as a covariate in every model including the null -- this provides first-order control. However, during the Gannon storm, thermospheric expansion effectively lowers the iso-density surface; the altitude covariate is static and linear, so storm-time orbital contraction is not fully controlled. This is a disclosed, partial confound. (C) Composition change -- THE STRONGEST PHYSICAL CONFOUND and the one the instrument did not address: during the Gannon storm, the O/N2 ratio drops sharply in the equatorial thermosphere, changing mean molecular mass and thereby density independently of both F107 and Dst. Both the additive f(F107)+g(Dst) and the joint f(F107)+g(Dst)+h(F107*Dst) are wrong model classes for the storm window -- they lack a composition state variable. This is confirmed by the data: in the storm week (L-med|lin), the additive model saves -2.03 b/h (WORSE than the null), meaning neither model meaningfully compresses the storm density. The anti-synergy verdict in the storm window is therefore TWO WRONG MODELS dueling, not a meaningful compression comparison. HOWEVER, the overall anti-synergy verdict is NOT rescued by this attack: of the 3,576 valid hours, only 168 are in the storm week. The other 3,408 hours (quiet, quiet_pre, quiet_post, disturbed_other) all show negative synergy delta in linear cells, with the additive consistently beating the joint. Excluding the storm week entirely does not change the sign or magnitude of the main finding.

attacks.target: LEAKAGE: block split actually leak-free given rho1=0.983 autocorrelation?
attacks.detail: The AR(1)-effective sample size is n*(1-rho1)/(1+rho1) = 3576 * 0.017/1.983 = 31 effective independent observations. Decorrelation time is approximately 1/(1-rho1) = 59 hours. The block bootstrap uses L=72h blocks, which is borderline (72h is only 1.2x the decorrelation time). Moving-block bootstrap at this length provides approximate but not guaranteed coverage. The 95% CI [−4,457, −468] bits at L-med|lin is entirely anti-synergy even at the favorable 97.5th percentile endpoint. The upper bound of -468 bits is approximately 33x the AIC penalty for the interaction parameters and 8x the BIC penalty -- meaning the CI would need to be dramatically wider (a factor of ~30 wider) to contain zero. With a larger block size L=168h (1 week), the CI would widen but the sign is unlikely to flip given this margin. On target leakage: none exists -- lag features are computed from the driver series (F107, Dst), not from lagged y. The pattern of using driver lags from the full series for a time-series regression is standard practice and does not constitute leakage of the holdout target. VERDICT: the leakage concern is real (borderline block size, rho1=0.983 inflates absolute NLL) but does not threaten the anti-synergy conclusion given the size of the margin.

attacks.target: THE FLIP: is the quiet-vs-storm dominance flip just a variance-ratio artifact?
attacks.detail: This is the strongest surviving attack and it PARTIALLY succeeds. The variance-ratio numbers are stark: Dst std in storm = 0.981 (Dst/100 units) vs 0.140 in quiet (7.0x ratio); F107 std in storm = 0.010 vs 0.088 in quiet (0.12x ratio). A pure variance-ratio model using the QUIET-FITTED coefficients (beta_F107 = 0.937, beta_Dst = -0.288) predicts the flip with the same coefficients: in quiet, |beta_F * f_std_q| = 0.082 > |beta_D * d_std_q| = 0.033 (F dominates); in storm, |beta_F * f_std_s| = 0.009 < |beta_D * d_std_s| = 0.282 (Dst dominates). The variance-ratio alone, with NO change in the underlying physics, fully accounts for the flip qualitatively. Additional evidence: the storm-window OLS F107 coefficient is physically nonsensical (beta_F107_storm = -4.59, negative, meaning density decreases with EUV), which is impossible and confirms that the 168-hour storm OLS is overfitting on F107's near-zero storm-window variance (std = 0.010 log units). The standardized regression check is inconclusive precisely because F107 has negligible within-storm variance, making normalization amplify noise by a factor of ~9. What a GENUINE dominance flip would require: (a) showing the standardized Dst coefficient exceeds the standardized F107 coefficient in the storm, with F107 variance held at its quiet-period level, i.e., a matched-variance comparison; or (b) independent stealth-CME cases (Dst storm without F107 co-elevation) that still show Dst dominance. The current data cannot distinguish the variance-ratio explanation from genuine mechanism change. This is the strongest surviving critique because it does not require reversing the synergy verdict -- it challenges the physical interpretation of the flip observable, which is the most scientifically interesting positive result of the instrument.

adversary.strongest_surviving_critique: THE FLIP as variance-ratio artifact (Attack 6). The quiet-to-storm dominance reversal -- F10.7 dominant (6.8:1 bits ratio) in quiet, Dst dominant (3.9:1) in storm -- is fully explained by a pure input-variance shift without any change in the underlying coupling coefficients. Dst std increases 7x from quiet to storm; F107 std decreases 8x (F107 is nearly constant at 218-228 sfu during the Gannon main phase). A single set of quiet-fitted coefficients, applied to storm-period input variances, predicts both the flip direction and approximate magnitude. The storm-window OLS beta_F107 = -4.59 (physically impossible sign) confirms the 168-hour storm window is too small and F107 too constrained to produce reliable coefficient estimates. The frame-flip observable -- advertised as the most meaningful positive finding of the instrument -- cannot currently be distinguished from a trivial variance-budget reallocation. Ruling it out as genuine requires either matched-variance evaluation (hold both driver variances equal and check coefficients) or stealth-CME cases from DONKI where Dst storms occur without co-elevated F107. Until that test is run, the flip observable should be listed as variance-consistent, not driver-dominance-confirmed."

synthesis.one_line: Anti-synergy: the proper additive law f(F10.7)+g(Dst) beats the joint interaction model in all 6 engine cells by 1698–2833 bits (linear cells); the frame-flip direction is confirmed but partially explained by variance-ratio mechanics, not physics alone.
synthesis.synergy_reading:
NO SYNERGY. ANTI-SYNERGY across all 6 engine cells (3 lag budgets x 2 model families). The F10.7 x Dst interaction term costs 1753 bits of data-fit at L-med|lin BEFORE any model-bit penalty is applied. NLL synergy delta = -2073 bits (-0.58 b/h); 95% CI block-bootstrap L=72h: [-4457, -468] — entirely anti-synergy. Permutation floor p95 = -272 bits; observed delta is well inside the anti-synergy tail, not near the floor. Engine-calibration band (linear cells only): -1698 to -2833 bits; sign unanimous. LZMA delta at resolution floor (L-med|lin = 0 bits exactly); NLL is the load-bearing scorer.

What the additive law says: F10.7 carries genuine independent signal (partial corr with log-density conditioned on Dst = +0.634); Dst carries genuine independent signal conditioned on F10.7 (-0.630). The additive is not double-counting; the drivers are nearly uncorrelated overall (r = -0.129). The backfit is joint-OLS per gain_v2 discipline. Compression gain vs null: F10.7 marginal +6.9%, Dst marginal +2.2%, additive +8.6%, joint ~+0.4% (near-null).

Mechanism (adversary confirmed): the F10.7 x Dst product term is near-collinear with Dst alone during 96% of the window. During the Gannon storm, F10.7 was nearly constant (218–228 sfu, std 0.010 log units), so the interaction term is informationally redundant with Dst. VIF(Dst/100) = 1842, VIF(F107*Dst) = 1848. Ridge penalty shrinks the interaction direction toward zero; cross-validation then penalizes the overfitted training fold. In-sample: interaction buys +0.082 b/h. Out-of-sample: interaction loses -1.065 b/h. Textbook overfit.

Robustness: AR(1)-whitened scoring preserves anti-synergy sign (-611 bits whitened at L-med|lin). Purged 60/40 split (168-hour gap, decorrelation time ~22h) also anti-synergy (-1286 bits lin). Joint residual rho1 = 0.983 inflates absolute NLL values but is a shared confound for both models; relative ordering is stable.

Surviving adversary notes: (1) Collinearity — partial collinearity between the interaction term and Dst explains WHY the joint fails, but this SUPPORTS the anti-synergy verdict, not attacks it. (2) Model-bits — the loss holds in data-only bits; even at zero parameter cost the joint loses. (3) Lags — the additive and joint use identical lag sets; the missing lag argument cannot rescue synergy. (4) Physical confounds — altitude as linear covariate provides first-order control; storm-time O/N2 composition change is a disclosed uncontrolled confound but affects ~4.7% of hours and does not change the overall sign. (5) Leakage — ruled out by purged split. (6) The flip — partially survives, see frame_flip_reading.

The most important remaining confound: F10.7 was co-elevated (218–228 sfu) during the Gannon storm main phase (Dst < -200 nT, 22 hours). The interaction term conflates two simultaneously elevated additive drivers with genuine multiplicative coupling. The common-cause hypothesis (both drivers are projections of the same solar-state parent) is consistent with and partially evidenced by this co-elevation. The 2024-07-30 F10.7 outlier (412.9 sfu, no Dst response, probable radio burst) was capped at 300 sfu and partially excluded — it is the most informative natural test cell for the common-cause hypothesis and its exclusion is a disclosed gap.
synthesis.frame_flip_reading:
DIRECTION CONFIRMED in linear cells; MECHANISM AMBIGUOUS. The reversal is unanimous across L-small, L-med, and L-large linear configurations:

Quiet pre-storm (Mar–Apr 2024, n=1333h): F10.7 saves +0.909 b/h, Dst saves +0.133 b/h. F10.7 dominant, ratio 6.8:1.
Quiet all (F10.7 < 150 AND |Dst| < 30, n=3078h): F10.7 saves +0.621 b/h, Dst saves +0.154 b/h. F10.7 dominant, ratio 4.0:1.
Gannon storm week (2024-05-10..16, n=168h): F10.7 saves +0.127 b/h, Dst saves +0.500 b/h. Dst dominant, ratio 3.9:1 Dst/F10.7.
Quiet post-storm (Jun–Jul 2024, n=1703h): F10.7 saves +0.396 b/h, Dst saves +0.170 b/h. F10.7 dominant (reduced strength vs pre-storm), ratio 2.3:1.
Window-refit (models trained within-window, storm): Dst less-negative than F10.7 (-3.93 vs -4.90 b/h), direction consistent with Dst dominance.
-50 nT quiet threshold sensitivity: preserves F10.7 dominance in quiet window.

Adversary's strongest attack PARTIALLY succeeds: the variance-ratio mechanism fully accounts for the flip direction. Dst std in storm = 0.981 (Dst/100 units) vs 0.140 in quiet (7.0x ratio); F10.7 std in storm = 0.010 log units vs 0.088 quiet (0.12x ratio). A single set of quiet-fitted OLS coefficients applied to storm-period input variances predicts both the flip direction and approximate magnitude — from variance reallocation alone, with no change in physics.

What survives: scale-free partial correlations (altitude removed, each driver at own best lag) show Dst's coupling GENUINELY strengthens in the storm window. Quiet partial-r(Dst) = 0.424 vs storm partial-r(Dst) = 0.850 — the storm Dst coupling exceeds the 90th percentile of 300 random quiet windows. Dst does couple more strongly to density in the Gannon storm. This half of the flip is real.

What does not survive robustly: F10.7 quiet-dominance is not robust — F10.7 wins only ~55% of random quiet windows in partial-correlation analysis; Dst-dominance appears in 45%. The F10.7 storm-window number rests on near-zero dynamic range (std = 0.010 log units); the storm OLS beta_F107 = -4.59 is physically impossible (negative sign) and confirms overfitting on that constrained variance.

Correct characterization: the flip observable is real in its Dst half (Dst genuinely couples harder in storm) and variance-driven in its F10.7 half (F10.7 looks dominant in quiet partly because Dst is nearly stationary there). The observable cannot currently be distinguished from pure variance-budget reallocation without a matched-variance test (hold both driver variances equal and check coefficients separately) or stealth-CME cases (Dst storm without co-elevated F10.7). It should be listed as variance-consistent, not driver-dominance-confirmed, pending those tests.
dead_children: "Joint density|(F10.7,Dst) synergizes beyond the additive law" — DEAD 2026-06-13. Reversed in all 6 engine cells (3 lag budgets x 2 model families), both NLL and LZMA scoring, leak-free purged split, AR(1)-whitened scoring. The interaction term costs bits even before model-bit penalty.

"The quiet-sun F10.7 dominance is a robust physical signal" — DEMOTED 2026-06-13. F10.7 wins only ~55% of random quiet windows in partial-correlation analysis; dominance is partly a variance-ratio artifact (Dst is near-stationary in quiet). Survives as: F10.7 carries more average independent signal than Dst over the study window, not as a framing-independent physical claim.

"Quadratic Dst terms improve storm-window fit" — DEAD 2026-06-13. Dst^2 catastrophically overfits the -406 nT Gannon extreme; storm-window quad scores are physically uninterpretable (mDst costs 154–314 b/h in quad cells during storm). Quadratic model family disqualified for storm-window analysis.

"The additive model is well-specified across all regimes" — DEMOTED 2026-06-13. Storm window (n=168): additive saves -2.03 b/h (WORSE than null). # S1 — drag x solar synergy: FINDINGS

**Status (2026-06-13): ANTI-SYNERGY verdict; FRAME-FLIP directionally confirmed, mechanism ambiguous.**
Register: exploratory INSTRUMENT, 0.99-not-Boolean. Real fetched data only. No fabrication anywhere in the chain.

---

## 1. The question

Does the JOINT law `density|(F10.7, Dst)` compress held-out thermospheric density more than a properly-specified additive baseline `f(F10.7) + g(Dst)`? The additive baseline is a joint-OLS backfit (gain_v2 discipline: NEVER the naive sum of separately-fitted marginals). Model bits counted. The frame observable: does driver DOMINANCE flip quiet-sun vs storm (Gannon 2024-05-10/11)?

**Framed phenomenon:** GRACE-FO orbit-averaged neutral density, 2024-03-01 to 2024-07-31, hourly. **Inferred:** next-hour held-out log-density, given (F10.7 lags, Dst lags, altitude covariate).

---

## 2. Numbers table (committed, L-med|lin is the anchor cell)

## 3. Frame-flip numbers (L-med|lin)

| window | n hours | F10.7 b/h | Dst b/h | dominant | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| quiet pre-storm (Mar–Apr 2024) | 1 333 | +0.909 | +0.133 | F10.7 | 6.8:1 |

Flip unanimous across all three linear lag configurations. Window-refit corroborates direction (storm Dst less negative than F10.7: -3.93 vs -4.90 b/h). Scale-free partial-corr: storm partial-r(Dst) = 0.850 vs quiet 0.424 — Dst coupling genuinely strengthens in storm (90th pct of 300 random quiet windows). Adversary partial-succeeds: the flip direction is also consistent with pure variance-ratio mechanics (Dst std 7x higher in storm; F10.7 std 0.12x quiet level).

---

## 4. Synergy gate verdict

**ANTI-SYNERGY.** The interaction term costs 1753 bits of data-fit before any model-bit penalty. The additive law is the better compressor in all 6 cells, under leak-free holdout, under AR(1)-whitened scoring (-611 bits whitened), under a purged 60/40 split (-1286 bits). The weld between the two driver parents is ADDITIVE; no multiplicative coupling detectable at this channel resolution and driver-variance regime.

Mechanism: F10.7 nearly constant during the Gannon storm (std = 0.010 log units, range 218–228 sfu); the F10.7 x Dst product term is near-collinear with Dst alone during the one major storm event. VIF(F107*Dst) = 1848. The common-cause hypothesis (both drivers are downstream projections of the same solar active region) is consistent with this structure and with the co-elevation of F10.7 and Dst during the Gannon event.

---

## 5. Philosopher's surviving reframes

**The weld reading.** Anti-synergy is not a failure of the parents-produce-W_C formalism; it is what the formalism predicts when the weld is additive. Each parent law contributes compression independently; the child inherits both membranes. The interaction term attempts to model a weld-coupling not present at this resolution; it finds noise. This is a strong instance of the additive join — the null case of the formalism, which is the hardest baseline to beat.

**Frame-relativity vs regime change.** The flip is consistent with two hypotheses that the data cannot distinguish: (a) frame-relativity — the information budget shifts (Dst unsaturates, F10.7 saturates its contribution), physics unchanged; (b) genuine regime change — coupling coefficients change inside the storm. Separating these requires fitting coefficients with matched driver variances.

**Common-cause (unresolved).** F10.7 and Dst may both be downstream of a single solar-state variable. The anti-synergy result is consistent with this: two projections of a common parent each carry signal, but their product term adds nothing because the parent's structure is already captured additively.

---

1. What is the minimum-entropy representation of the common solar-state parent, and does density compress more against that latent parent than against either proxy?

2. The rho1 = 0.983 residual is the loudest number and is treated as a caveat. What law models the residual structure — AR(1), thermospheric relaxation parametric (known timescales: photoionization hours; O/N2 composition days; NO cooling recovery days), or a storm-hysteresis state variable? The current best model explains ~2% of available compression.

3. Is the altitude covariate absorbing the storm signal? The linear static altitude coefficient may systematically mis-correct storm-time orbital contraction. Test: interact altitude with Dst; compare frame-flip ratios.

---

**Stealth-CME falsification:** Run the gate on Dst storms where F10.7 was NOT co-elevated. DONKI event list https://kauai.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/search/ (auth-free REST JSON). If FISM2 marginal > F10.7 marginal AND synergy delta less negative, the anti-synergy verdict is partly a proxy-quality artifact.
